blocks.text: To write a job once and use it many times we define a **function**. It starts with `fn` and has a name and parentheses. `main` is a function too; we call the other functions from inside `main`.

A function can take information (**parameters**) and give a result back (`return`). The parameter's type is written after `:`, the return type after `->`. `i32` is the whole-number type; you will learn types in the next chapter.

blocks.prompt: Finish the function `square`: it should return the square of the number it receives (the number times itself).

blocks.q: Which word gives a result back from a function?
blocks.why: `return` sends the value back to the caller; `print` only writes to the screen.
